title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 13.

questions.question: Who did David consult with before making his decision about the ark?
options: The captains of thousands and hundreds, and every leader
questions.correctAnswer: The captains of thousands and hundreds, and every leader
questions.explanation: David consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader before proceeding (1 Chronicles 13:1).

questions.question: What was David's proposal to the congregation of Israel regarding the ark?
options: To send abroad to all Israel and gather the priests and Levites to bring the ark back to them
To destroy the ark as it was no longer needed
To leave the ark where it was permanently
To build a new ark for the house of David
questions.correctAnswer: To send abroad to all Israel and gather the priests and Levites to bring the ark back to them
questions.explanation: David proposed to send abroad to their brethren everywhere in Israel along with the priests and Levites to gather themselves so they could bring back the ark (1 Chronicles 13:2).

questions.question: Why did David say they had not enquired of the ark in the days of Saul?
options: Because they had not asked God about moving the ark before
Because the ark was lost during Saul's reign
Because Saul had hidden the ark
Because the priests refused to move the ark
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had not asked God about moving the ark before
questions.explanation: David said they had not enquired at the ark in the days of Saul, meaning they did not seek God's guidance about moving it then (1 Chronicles 13:3).

questions.question: How did the congregation of Israel respond to David's proposal about the ark?
options: They all agreed it was right and would do so
They were divided on the matter
They asked for more time to consider
questions.correctAnswer: They all agreed it was right and would do so
questions.explanation: All the congregation said they would do as David proposed because it was right in their eyes (1 Chronicles 13:4).

questions.question: From where to where did David gather Israel to bring the ark?
options: From Shihor of Egypt to the entering of Hemath
From the wilderness of Paran to the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: From Shihor of Egypt to the entering of Hemath
questions.explanation: David gathered all Israel from Shihor of Egypt even unto the entering of Hemath to bring the ark (1 Chronicles 13:5).

questions.question: To which city did David and all Israel go to bring up the ark of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Baalah, which is Kirjathjearim
questions.explanation: David and all Israel went to Baalah, also called Kirjathjearim, to bring up the ark (1 Chronicles 13:6).

questions.question: How was the ark of God transported from the house of Abinadab?
options: In a new cart driven by Uzza and Ahio
By priests carrying it on their shoulders
On a wooden platform carried by Levites
questions.correctAnswer: In a new cart driven by Uzza and Ahio
questions.explanation: The ark was carried in a new cart out of the house of Abinadab, with Uzza and Ahio driving the cart (1 Chronicles 13:7).

questions.question: What instruments did David and all Israel use while playing before God?
options: Harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets
questions.correctAnswer: Harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets
questions.explanation: David and all Israel played before God with singing and various instruments including harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets (1 Chronicles 13:8).

questions.question: What happened when the oxen stumbled at the threshingfloor of Chidon?
options: Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark
The ark was dropped and broken
questions.correctAnswer: Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark
questions.explanation: When the oxen stumbled, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark (1 Chronicles 13:9).

questions.question: What was the consequence of Uzza touching the ark?
options: The LORD was angry and smote him, causing his death
He was praised for protecting the ark
He was made priest of the ark
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD was angry and smote him, causing his death
questions.explanation: The anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzza because he put his hand on the ark, and he died there before God (1 Chronicles 13:10).

questions.question: True or False: David was pleased with the death of Uzza and immediately brought the ark into the city of David.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David was displeased and afraid because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza, so he did not bring the ark into the city of David immediately (1 Chronicles 13:11-13).

questions.question: What name was given to the place where Uzza was struck down?
questions.correctAnswer: Perezuzza
questions.explanation: The place was called Perezuzza because the LORD made a breach upon Uzza there (1 Chronicles 13:11).

questions.question: Where did David place the ark instead of bringing it to his city?
options: In the house of Obededom the Gittite
questions.correctAnswer: In the house of Obededom the Gittite
questions.explanation: David did not bring the ark to the city of David but carried it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite (1 Chronicles 13:13).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD blessed the house of Obededom and all that he had while the ark remained there for three months.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The ark remained in the house of Obededom for three months, and the LORD blessed his house and all he had (1 Chronicles 13:14).

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Chronicles 13, David asked for the LORD's approval before sending abroad to gather the people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David said if it seemed good to the congregation and was of the LORD, then they would send abroad to gather the people (1 Chronicles 13:2).

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Where did David and all Israel go to bring up the ark of God, according to 1 Chronicles 13?
questions.correctAnswer: Baalah, that is Kirjathjearim
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:6 states that David and all Israel went up to Baalah, also known as Kirjathjearim, to bring up the ark of God.

questions.question: Who were the two men driving the new cart that carried the ark of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Uzza and Ahio
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 13:7, Uzza and Ahio drove the new cart that carried the ark of God from the house of Abinadab.

questions.question: How did David and all Israel express their worship before God as they brought the ark?
options: With singing, harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets
questions.correctAnswer: With singing, harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:8 describes David and all Israel playing before God with all their might and using singing and various musical instruments in worship.

questions.question: What caused Uzza to put forth his hand to hold the ark?
questions.correctAnswer: The oxen stumbled
questions.explanation: As stated in 1 Chronicles 13:9, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark because the oxen stumbled while carrying it.

questions.question: What was the consequence of Uzza putting his hand to the ark?
options: The LORD was angry and struck him dead
He was praised for protecting the ark
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD was angry and struck him dead
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:10 explains that the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzza because he touched the ark, and he died there before God.

questions.question: Why did David become displeased after Uzza's death?
options: Because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza
Because the people started to rebel
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:11 states David was displeased because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza, which refers to the sudden death of Uzza when he touched the ark.

questions.question: What name was given to the place where Uzza died, and why?
options: Perezuzza, because the LORD made a breach there
questions.correctAnswer: Perezuzza, because the LORD made a breach there
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:11 records that the place was called Perezuzza because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza there.

questions.question: How did David respond to the fear of bringing the ark into the city of David?
options: He carried the ark aside into the house of Obededom
He immediately took the ark into the city
He sent the ark back to Kirjathjearim
He consulted the priests for instructions
questions.correctAnswer: He carried the ark aside into the house of Obededom
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:12-13 recount that David was afraid and so brought not the ark home but carried it into the house of Obededom the Gittite.

questions.question: What blessing came to the house of Obededom during the time the ark remained there?
options: The LORD blessed the house of Obededom and all that he had
The house was destroyed by a plague
The family was cursed with famine
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD blessed the house of Obededom and all that he had
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 13:14, the ark remained with Obededom's family for three months, and the LORD blessed the house and all that he had.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 13:9-10 teach about obedience and reverence in handling holy things?
options: Improper handling of holy things can bring God's judgment
Holy things can be handled casually
Human strength can protect sacred objects
God does not concern Himself with the manner of handling the ark
questions.correctAnswer: Improper handling of holy things can bring God's judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 show Uzza was struck down for touching the ark, teaching the importance of strict obedience and reverence toward God's holy things.

questions.question: How does the reaction of David after Uzza's death in verse 12 show a lesson on fear and trust in God?
options: David's fear made him pause and reconsider how to bring the ark properly
David immediately ignored God's judgment and proceeded
David blamed Uzza for the accident
David sent the ark away forever
questions.correctAnswer: David's fear made him pause and reconsider how to bring the ark properly
questions.explanation: Verse 12 highlights David's fear of God and his uncertainty about bringing the ark home, teaching believers to approach God with reverence and careful trust.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 13:6, what is the significance of the ark dwelling 'between the cherubims'?
options: It signifies God's presence and holiness residing on the ark
It means the ark belonged to the cherubim
It was a decorative feature only
It was a symbol of Israel's military power
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies God's presence and holiness residing on the ark
questions.explanation: Verse 6 indicates that the ark is where the LORD dwells between the cherubims, symbolizing God's presence and holiness.

questions.question: True or False: David consulted only with the priests before deciding to bring the ark to Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:1 shows that David consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds and every leader, not only priests.

questions.question: True or False: The congregation of Israel agreed to bring the ark back to them because they believed it was right before the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:4 states that all the congregation said they would do so because the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.

questions.question: True or False: The ark was carried by Levites on their shoulders as commanded by the Law.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 13:7, the ark was carried on a new cart driven by Uzza and Ahio, which was contrary to the Law's instruction for Levites to carry it on poles.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 13.

questions.question: Why was the place called Perezuzza?
options: Because the LORD made a breach upon Uzza
Because David built a city there
Because the ark was placed there
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD made a breach upon Uzza
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:11 states that David was displeased because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza, and therefore the place was called Perezuzza.

questions.question: What was David's emotional reaction after Uzza's death?
questions.correctAnswer: He was displeased
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:11 explains that David was displeased because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzza.

questions.question: What question did David ask himself after the incident with Uzza?
options: How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?
Where should we build the temple?
Who will carry the ark next?
questions.correctAnswer: How shall I bring the ark of God home to me?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:12 records David's fear and his question about how he could bring the ark of God home after the incident with Uzza.

questions.question: Where did David place the ark after he did not bring it to the city of David?
options: In the house of Obededom the Gittite
questions.correctAnswer: In the house of Obededom the Gittite
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:13 states that David carried the ark aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite instead of bringing it to the city of David.

questions.question: How long did the ark remain in the house of Obededom?
questions.correctAnswer: Three months
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 13:14, the ark of God remained with the family of Obededom for three months.

questions.question: What happened to the house of Obededom while the ark was there?
options: It was blessed by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: It was blessed by the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:14 notes that the LORD blessed the house of Obededom and all that he had during the ark's stay.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the narrative of Uzza's death and the ark's temporary stay with Obededom?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter opens with the intent to bring the ark to David, interrupted by Uzza's death, and closes with the ark staying safely in Obededom's house, creating a literary inclusio framing the narrative (1 Chronicles 13:1-14).

questions.question: The Hebrew meaning of the word 'Perezuzza' refers to what concept?
questions.correctAnswer: Breakthrough or breach
questions.explanation: The name 'Perezuzza' derives from Hebrew roots meaning 'breach' or 'breakthrough,' referencing God's breach upon Uzza (1 Chronicles 13:11).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God's holiness and the danger of mishandling the ark as seen in 1 Chronicles 13?
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 4:15
questions.explanation: Numbers 4:15 prescribes the proper handling of the ark by Levites, highlighting God's holiness and the danger of improper contact, which is directly related to the incident in 1 Chronicles 13:9-10.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects on the holiness and reverence due to God, similar to the fear David had after Uzza's death?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 12:28
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:28 discusses receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, leading to reverent fear and worship, echoing David's fear of God in 1 Chronicles 13:12.

questions.question: What was the original method used to transport the ark that led to Uzza's fatal mistake?
questions.correctAnswer: In a new cart
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:7 states that the ark was carried in a new cart driven by Uzza and Ahio, which led to Uzza touching the ark when the oxen stumbled.

questions.question: True or False: David immediately brought the ark into the city of David after the incident with Uzza.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:13 records that David did not bring the ark into the city of David immediately after Uzza's death but placed it in Obededom's house.

questions.question: True or False: The congregation of Israel fully agreed with David's plan to bring the ark back.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:4 states that all the congregation said they would do so because it was right in the eyes of all the people.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also records David bringing the ark to Jerusalem and shows the continuation of this narrative?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 6
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6 continues the story of David bringing the ark to Jerusalem, showing the fulfillment following the incident described in 1 Chronicles 13.

questions.question: What role did Uzza and Ahio play during the transportation of the ark?
options: They drove the cart carrying the ark
They led the singing and worship
They guarded the ark from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They drove the cart carrying the ark
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:7 specifies that Uzza and Ahio drove the cart that carried the ark out of the house of Abinadab.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David's consultation with the captains and leaders before moving the ark indicate about his leadership approach?
options: He acted independently without seeking counsel
He sought collective agreement and divine approval
questions.correctAnswer: He sought collective agreement and divine approval
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:1 shows David consulting captains and leaders, indicating he valued collective input and sought to ensure the action was right before proceeding.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 13:2, what was the theological reason David wanted to send for the priests and Levites to gather?
options: To ensure the move would be approved by the LORD
To collect taxes for the journey
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure the move would be approved by the LORD
questions.explanation: David’s desire to send for priests and Levites was to confirm that the move was according to the LORD’s will, showing reverence for divine approval as the basis for action (1 Chronicles 13:2).

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by David’s acknowledgment that he had not inquired of the ark in Saul’s days?
options: Ignoring God’s guidance leads to failure
The ark was irrelevant in Saul’s time
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring God’s guidance leads to failure
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 13:3 highlights the importance of seeking God’s direction through the ark, teaching that neglecting divine guidance leads to missteps.

questions.question: From which geographical extent did David gather Israel to bring the ark according to 1 Chronicles 13:5?
options: From Shihor of Egypt to the entering of Hemath
From Mount Sinai to Mount Zion
questions.correctAnswer: From Shihor of Egypt to the entering of Hemath
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows the comprehensive gathering of Israel from the southern border (Shihor of Egypt) to the northern border (Hemath), illustrating the unity and extent of God’s people under David.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD’s dwelling 'between the cherubims' on the ark as described in 1 Chronicles 13:6?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and glory
questions.explanation: The LORD dwelling between the cherubims signifies His holiness and glory manifesting in a special presence, emphasizing divine majesty (1 Chronicles 13:6).

questions.question: What doctrinal error is illustrated by Uzza’s action of touching the ark to steady it?
options: Presumption and irreverence toward the holy
questions.correctAnswer: Presumption and irreverence toward the holy
questions.explanation: Uzza’s act of touching the ark without divine command shows presumption and irreverence, violating God’s holiness rules (1 Chronicles 13:9-10).

questions.question: How does the LORD’s reaction to Uzza's act reveal an attribute of God?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and justice
questions.explanation: God’s immediate judgment on Uzza for touching the ark shows His holiness and justice, emphasizing the sacredness of divine commands (1 Chronicles 13:10).

questions.question: What theological significance does the naming of the place 'Perezuzza' have in the narrative?
options: It marks a breach or failure caused by human disobedience
It refers to a peaceful gathering
questions.correctAnswer: It marks a breach or failure caused by human disobedience
questions.explanation: The place name 'Perezuzza' (meaning 'breach of Uzza') memorializes the consequence of failing to respect God’s holiness (1 Chronicles 13:11).

questions.question: What does David’s fear after the incident with Uzza teach about reverence for God?
options: Reverence is unnecessary for God’s presence
Fear of God leads to cautious worship and obedience
Fear should be avoided in worship
God’s presence can be taken lightly
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of God leads to cautious worship and obedience
questions.explanation: David’s fear (1 Chronicles 13:12) shows that reverence leads to careful respect for God’s holiness and commands in worship.

questions.question: Why did David choose to place the ark in the house of Obededom rather than bringing it to the city of David immediately?
options: Because the ark had brought blessing to Obededom’s household
Because David was afraid after Uzza’s death
Because the city of David was destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: Because David was afraid after Uzza’s death
questions.explanation: David’s fear after Uzza’s death led him to place the ark temporarily in Obededom’s house rather than bringing it directly to his city (1 Chronicles 13:12-13).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is illustrated by the ark remaining in Obededom’s house for three months and the LORD blessing his household?
options: God’s blessing is unrelated to His presence
God’s presence brings blessing to the faithful
God’s blessing depends on human wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence brings blessing to the faithful
questions.explanation: The ark’s presence in Obededom’s house resulting in blessing (1 Chronicles 13:14) typifies that God’s presence brings blessing to those who honor Him.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth emerges from David’s initial consultation (verse 1) and the people’s unanimous agreement (verse 4) regarding bringing the ark?
options: Human consensus is more important than God’s will
Leadership and congregational unity are essential in pursuing God’s revealed will
Only kings can decide spiritual matters
The ark’s movement was a political strategy
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership and congregational unity are essential in pursuing God’s revealed will
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 4 together teach that God’s work requires both wise leadership consultation and the congregation’s united agreement, reflecting orderly worship and obedience.

questions.question: How do verses 5-6 together emphasize the significance of God’s covenant presence among Israel?
options: They emphasize God dwelling among His people specifically in the ark, symbolizing covenant presence
They focus on David’s military conquest
questions.correctAnswer: They emphasize God dwelling among His people specifically in the ark, symbolizing covenant presence
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe gathering Israel to bring the ark dwelling 'between the cherubims,' underscoring God’s covenantal presence central to Israel’s identity.

questions.question: What theological insight is drawn by comparing Uzza’s death (verse 10) and the ark’s blessing on Obededom’s house (verse 14)?
options: God’s presence is arbitrary in blessing and judgment
God is just and holy, punishing irreverence but blessing reverence
God does not care about how the ark is handled
The ark has no spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: God is just and holy, punishing irreverence but blessing reverence
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 14 show God’s holiness in judgment (Uzza’s death) and His blessing on reverence (Obededom’s household), revealing divine justice and grace.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s killing of Uzza was unjust and overly harsh. What does 1 Chronicles 13:9-10 actually teach about God’s holiness and human responsibility?
options: God is indifferent to human actions
God’s holiness demands strict respect for His commands, and human presumption incurs serious consequences
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands strict respect for His commands, and human presumption incurs serious consequences
questions.explanation: The passage reveals that God's holiness is absolute and humans must not presume to treat sacred things lightly; Uzza’s death is a solemn reminder of divine justice (1 Chronicles 13:9-10).
